panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Renal PAS histology from a human patient showing the lobular MPGN pattern and peripheral glomerular basement membrane dense deposits characteristic of dense deposit disease. [raw subtype: type II membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis] b: High-magnification renal PAS image demonstrates dense material along peripheral glomerular basement membranes, a characteristic manifestation of dense deposit disease. [raw subtype: type II membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis] c: Renal immunofluorescence from the reported dense deposit disease patient shows segmental pseudolinear and granular IgM deposits along peripheral capillary walls; this is a specific captioned renal manifestation, although the allowed vocabulary lacks an IgM-specific finding. [raw subtype: type II membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis]

panels.figure_caption: (a) Type II membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis characterized by mesangial matrix and cellular increases is responsible for a lobular accentuation associated with a diffuse and intense staining of the peripheral basement membrane (periodic acid-Schiff [PAS], magnification [G]: ×200). (b) The diffuse and intense staining of the peripheral basement membrane indicates the presence of dense deposit material (PAS, G ×2000). (c) Immunofluorescence techniques show segmental pseudo linear and granular IgM deposits along the peripheral capillary wall (fluorescein isothiocyanate anti-IgM, G ×100).

findings.label: Dome-shaped sub-RPE deposits on OCT
findings.evidence: Caption states: 'OCT cut through drusen showing preservation of the RPE and photoreceptors, with thickening of Bruch’s membrane', consistent with sub-RPE dome-shaped deposits of dense deposit disease

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: En face ophthalmic image of a human patient with dense deposit disease, showing multiple posterior pole subretinal drusenoid deposits consistent with the disease's known ocular manifestation. No controls, other diseases, or non-patient content are present. B: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) ophthalmic image of the same human patient with dense deposit disease, demonstrating Bruch’s membrane thickening with intact RPE and photoreceptors, consistent with the disease's subretinal drusenoid deposits. No other diseases or non-patient content are present.

panels.figure_caption: OCT cut through drusen showing preservation of the RPE and photoreceptors, with thickening of Bruch’s membrane
in_text_mentions: At the most recent visit (October 2016) the patient’s BCVA was recorded in the right eye as 49 ETDRS letters and awareness of hand movements only in the left eye. The fundus examination demonstrated multiple subretinal drusenoid deposits, which were autofluorescent, mainly at the posterior pole. Careful review of the OCT images demonstrated that the deposits were in Bruch’s membrane, with an intact Retinal Pigment Epithelium (RPE) (Fig. 5).Fig. 5OCT cut through drusen showing preservation of the RPE and photoreceptors, with thickening of Bruch’s membrane
